messages:
Maya: quick sync after the RFC meeting. we agreed caching is valuable at the edge for inference latency, but we need concrete invalidation guarantees. do we want push invalidation, versioned keys, or hybrid?
Ian: hybrid. prefer versioned keys + event bump. push-only is fragile across flaky webhooks, TTL-only is slow for revocations. versioned keys give deterministic invalidation when we increment the project-level version.
Priya: agree on versioned keys. add a soft TTL so accidental missed bumps don't keep stale grants forever. also think about token binding: user tokens without project scope should never be used for cross-project calls even if cached.
Zach: propose key shape:
```
key = "auth:proj:{proj}:v{proj_v}:actor:{actor}:perm:{perm}:route:{route}"
TTL_default = 20s
```
proj_v is central per-project auth version. increment on effective permission changes.
Leila: question: where do we store proj_v? central redis vs strongly consistent store? Redis INCR is fine but ensure monotonicity across regions. use a leadered redis or a small central control plane store with cross-region replication.
Ian: central small Redis is fine for control plane; edges poll minimal metadata. algorithm:
1) edge receives request -> looks for local cache hit for key with current local proj_v
2) if miss -> fetch proj_v from central (cheap), then evaluate policy and store local cache with that proj_v
3) on bump -> central INCR proj_v, edges will miss next time and re-eval
This bounds staleness to TTL + propagation.
Priya: webhook schema for auth changes (POST /hooks/auth-change): fields = [project_id, changed_permissions[], bump_reason, bump_if_affects_inference (bool)]. we only bump proj_v when bump_if_affects_inference is true to avoid thrash.
authbot: perf update: staging run 2026-03-20T09:12Z - adding local cache + proj_v check with TTL 20s reduced p99 by 22%.
Maya: good. another risk: cross-region routing. if request A hits edge-1 and gets proj_v=5, then a role change increments proj_v->6 in central, but edge-2 still has 5 until it next fetches. we need to ensure no long window where revoked actor can call. mitigation: lower TTL for critical perms (model.deploy, model.call) to 5s and increase for read-only perms.
Zach: also add fast-path deny: if token includes explicit 'revoked' claim or a token revocation list (TRL) entry, check TRL on every request (small bloom filter locally updated). revocations should write to TRL and trigger a lightweight push to edges.
Ian: add header on failure for client UX: x-auth-retry-after-proj-v -> include current proj_v so client can optionally retry after refresh or surface message. for project-mismatch return 403 + x-auth-reason:project-mismatch.
Leila: logging/telemetry: emit metrics auth.cache_hit, auth.local_proj_v, auth.central_proj_v_fetch_ms, auth.eval_ms. add audit event when a cached allow is used for decision, include proj_v.
Priya: tests: (1) cross-project token reuse must fail. (2) bump propagation: after bump central proj_v, within 2s 90% of edges should observe new proj_v on next fetch. (3) revocation bounce: TRL update causes immediate denies.
Maya: risks: webhook storms could cause massive INCRs. mitigation: coalesce bumps per project with 10s window and only bump once if multiple relevant changes occur. store last_bump_ts to debounce.
Zach: docs: add small troubleshooting section: how to inspect proj_v (GET /controlplane/projects/:id/auth_v), how to force a bump, how to check TRL health.
Maya: action items: Maya -> write follow-up RFC with key patterns, TTL tiers, bump debounce, TRL contract. Ian -> implement cache wrapper prototype. Priya -> webhook schema + control plane API. Zach -> tests + TRL push consumer. Leila -> design cross-region proj_v store. target EOW for initial PRs.
rfc-bot: follow-up RFC draft: /rfc/authn-invalidation-hybrid (DRAFT) - Maya assigned.
